source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-33

procedures.title: Power steering hydraulic system: bleed
steps: Check belt tension and look for a bent or loose pulley; it must not wobble with the engine running.
Make sure the hoses touch nothing else, especially sheet metal and the exhaust manifold.
Check the oil level and fill as needed following steps 1 through 10.
Check for air in the oil; if present, try bleeding with steps 1 through 10. If the pump clearly will not bleed after a few tries, go to Hydraulic System Checks.
notes: Low oil level and air in the oil are the most common causes of objectionable pump noise.

procedures.title: Power steering fluid level: check
steps: Read the reservoir dipstick with the oil at operating temperature.
Fill if needed to the correct level with GM Power Steering Fluid, or if unavailable, Type A automatic transmission fluid marked AQ-ATF followed by a number and the suffix A.

procedures.title: Power steering gear (Corvette): adjust
steps: Adjust the gear used with Corvette power steering exactly as the manual steering gear.

procedures.title: Power steering pump belt: adjust tension
steps: Loosen the pivot bolt nut and the pump brace adjusting nut.
With the belt on, move the pump until gauge J-7316 shows the specified tension (see figure 60 in the manual).
Tighten the pump brace adjusting nut, then the pivot bolt nut.

specs.what: pump belt strand tension, new belt
pump belt strand tension, used belt

notes: Caution: never pry against the reservoir or pull on the filler neck to move the pump.

procedures.title: Power steering hydraulic system: test
steps: Before testing, check belt tension (125 lbs. new, 75 lbs. used, with gauge J-7316) and the drive pulley condition.
Test one shows whether the hydraulic parts are faulty; if it does, test two identifies which part.
Test one (circuit open): have the engine at normal operating temperature, the front tires at correct pressure, and the idle set to the Section 6 spec; all tests are run at idle.
